properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Anthony's VS Code work log (SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, entries of 2026-10-05 at lines 345-349 and 362-365). The ideas, in the reporter's words: "the installer could tar every store it can find (or print the backup line) before replacing the binary, or the recipe could say 'run this before `install.sh`'", and "name the copy from `reflow2-mcp --version`, and put the step before anything replaces the binary".

WHAT IS SETTLED, AND IS NOT REOPENED HERE: dec:backup-belongs-to-the-consumer (accepted 2026-08-06). reflow2 does not back a design up. It owes a documented update path, honest primitives, and saying so when something is off. The finding this answers is fact:root-cause-the-update-path-has-no-step-before-the-binary-is-replaced-2026-10-05. The documented path starts at the replacement, and on the one-shot doors the first open after it changes the store without a word.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) UPDATING.md GETS A "BEFORE YOU INSTALL" STEP. While the OLD binary is still in place: export each store you care about (or copy `.reflow2/`), and copy the binary under the name `reflow2-mcp --version` prints. Doc only, within the accepted boundary. SIZE: small.
(b) install.sh KEEPS THE BINARY IT REPLACES, as `reflow2-mcp.<old version>` (read from the old binary's `--version` before `install`), and prints the one-line rollback. Additive; nothing a running server sees changes. SIZE: small.
(c) install.sh PRINTS A BACKUP LINE (the export command) before it replaces anything, for the stores it can name. It knows of no stores, because the machine-wide install is project-agnostic. So the line is either generic, or read from places the installer does not own (hub configs, ~/.claude.json). SIZE: small for a generic line, moderate to find stores.
(d) THE INSTALLER COPIES EVERY STORE IT CAN FIND. This reopens dec:backup-belongs-to-the-consumer, so it is the owner's call, not this record's. SIZE: moderate. Cost: disk. The field machine has 20 stores, and the dev box is 82% full.
(e) A NEWER BINARY'S FIRST OPEN WRITES A PRE-UPGRADE EXPORT beside the store, before its repair runs. This is honest at the moment that matters, and works however the binary arrived. It also partly reopens the backup boundary, and costs disk on every upgrade. SIZE: moderate.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- A store survives an update by design, and the repair keeps everything any reader uses. A rollback point mostly protects against a downgrade, and on the door reflow2 does not check one (the side measurement in the same finding). So keeping the old binary invites the unguarded case unless the door's verdict is fixed first (fact:root-cause-every-one-shot-open-drops-the-version-verdict-and-the-repair-report-2026-10-05).
- The field upgrade did not go through install.sh at all, so (b) and (c) would not have reached it. Only (a) or (e) would have.
- Every option except (a) is new behaviour in an installer that a working user runs unattended ("my brother likes using as is"). (b) writes one more file, and (c) prints one more line. Neither changes reflow2's MCP behaviour.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED.
properties.name: OPEN — should installing a new reflow2 over an older one leave a rollback point before it replaces anything: a step in UPDATING.md, the old binary kept under its version, a printed backup line, or the stores themselves copied?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an open question from two field-log [friction] entries, under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05. Kept separate from dec:idea-what-the-first-open-after-an-upgrade-found-outlives-the-process-that-opened: this one is about the moment BEFORE the binary changes, and that one is about what is known AFTER.
